- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 2.0), model frequently overcorrects with a steep drop; cap forecast decline to 15–20% of peak for next 3 days.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show high forecast error, adjust next forecast toward historical 18-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early (first 5–7 days) and underestimates late (last 5–7 days); apply asymmetric smoothing: reduce early forecast by 15%, increase late forecast by 10%.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.33 or 0.00), model tends to underestimate; apply a 15–25% upward bias to forecast for next 7 days.
